title: Do good of your own free will, not only when commanded
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Jackson County on 1 August 1831, probably at Independence. Elders arriving in July found fewer than ten converts and a rough frontier town. Bishop Edward Partridge had disagreed with Joseph Smith over the quality of land being bought. That week Colesville Saints from Thompson, Ohio, also arrived. Many wanted to know the Lord’s will for them in the new gathering place.
summary: The revelation tells the elders that blessings come after much tribulation. It says they were sent to obey, to lay Zion’s foundation, and to prepare a feast for the poor. Edward Partridge is to judge in Israel and divide inheritances, but he must repent of unbelief. The Saints must keep the laws of the land. The Lord will not command in all things, so people should do much good of their own free will. Martin Harris is to lay his money before the bishop, and he and Phelps must repent. Sidney Rigdon is to describe Zion in writing and dedicate the land and temple site. Joseph Smith, Rigdon, and Cowdery are to return home, Ziba Peterson loses his office, and others preach on the way.

contextNote.title: Agents unto themselves
contextNote.text: The Saints in Missouri wanted detailed direction for a hard new place. Verse 26 answers that the Lord does not mean to command in all things. A servant who must be compelled in everything is called slothful. Verse 27 asks instead for people “anxiously engaged in a good cause” by free will. Verse 28 gives the reason: the power is in them, and they are agents unto themselves. Verse 29 draws the contrast with one who waits for orders and obeys with doubt. In this passage, being an agent means acting on one’s own to do good.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 58–59 draws out the call to act without waiting to be told. Verses 3–4 ask the Saints to wait for blessings, while verse 27 asks them to act now. What good cause could you begin this week without being asked?
reviewNote: Read all 65 verses. Official heading gives Zion, Jackson County, 1 August 1831, after the first Sabbath service and arrival of Colesville Saints. JSP historical introduction gave the few converts, the Partridge dispute, and the place as probably Independence. kirtland stands for the “church in Ohio” in v. 49 and the elders’ return.
